messages.text: Heads up: RiskEngine flagged the single-name concentration limit on one of the financials issuers at 94% utilization this morning. Still inside the limit but trending the wrong way after the Friday flows.
Thanks Paul. What's the hard limit again and who's the desk owner on that name? I want to know before the 3pm risk call.
Hard limit is 5% of the book on a single issuer, soft trigger at 4.5%. We're at 4.7%. Daniel's desk owns the position, I've already pinged him.
Separate but related: ReportingBI concentration dashboard is still showing last Thursday's sector buckets for me. Is anyone else seeing stale numbers or is it my cache?
Seeing the same on my end. The sector rollup looks one refresh behind the RiskEngine exposures. I'd trust RiskEngine for now.
On the credit side, our top 10 counterparty exposure is 38% of total lending commitments. Internal guideline is 40%, so we have thin headroom if the pipeline closes as scheduled.
That's tight. Phillip, can you model the pipeline closing in full and show me the pro forma by end of day? If we breach, I want a mitigation plan, e.g. participations or syndicating down.
Will do. I'll use the Q4 expected closings and run a haircut scenario too. John, can you pull the latest drawn vs undrawn splits?
Yep, on it. Undrawn revolvers are the swing factor, so I'll show both committed and expected-utilization views.
Update from Daniel: they can trim about $12M of the position this afternoon, which takes us back to roughly 4.3%. He wants to do it in two clips to limit market impact.
Good, go ahead. Please document the breach-avoidance rationale in the limit log so it's clean for the audit trail.
Confirmed the dashboard lag was a stale cache job on the BI side. Reran it and the sector buckets now match RiskEngine. I'll put a note in the channel if it happens again.
Trim is done, both clips filled. Single-name utilization is now at 4.3% of the 5% limit. Logging it now.
Pro forma is posted in the risk folder. Full pipeline close takes us to 40.6%, so a slight breach. A $15M participation sale would bring us back to about 39%. Happy to walk through it tomorrow.
